_about: Single source of truth for the Street Space Index. Both index.html and model/street_space.py read this file. Every number is either sourced (see 'sources') or an explicit, adjustable assumption.

mode_share_pct._note: Share of daily trips in Pune, approximated from the PMRDA Comprehensive Mobility Plan update (walking ~25%, PMPML ~10%, metro ~1%, auto+cab ~10%) and the 2025-26 cycling figure (3%). Two-wheeler/car split is an assumption.

occupancy._note: Average persons per vehicle. Assumptions; adjust with local survey data.

pcu._note: Passenger Car Units: how much lane space a vehicle takes relative to a car. Values in the range used in Indian urban practice (IRC:106); treat as adjustable.

footpath_usable._note: Fraction of drawn footpath width that is actually walkable (not encroached or obstructed). 1.0 = all of it. The ITDP audit found only 30% of pedestrians used footpaths on 11 Pune corridors, which suggests much lower real usability; the unusable part is counted as 'Medians, planters, encroached'.

itdp_corridors.label: ITDP 11-corridor respondents (2022)
itdp_corridors._note: ITDP surveyed 2,300 people on 11 corridors: 32% walked, 40% used public transport. The remaining 28% is split across 2W/car/auto in Pune's city ratio (assumption). Perception-survey respondents probably over-represent walkers and bus users.

itdp_audit.title: Pune's Walk & Cycle Analysis (ITDP India + PMC, Dec 2022)
itdp_audit.scope: 11 streets with right of way > 24 m, ~30 km, split into 500 m segments; design, observation and perception surveys; 2,300 people surveyed Oct-Nov 2022 at peak hours
findings: 70% of surveyed streets had footpaths, but only 30% of pedestrians used them
Encroachments and obstructions make footpaths and cycle tracks inaccessible
Streets built to Pune's Urban Street Design Guidelines performed better in all surveys
Survey respondents: 32% walked, 40% used public transport
itdp_audit.not_available_here: Per-street widths and footpath measurements are in the full PDF, which could not be retrieved programmatically. Road widths below remain assumptions except JM Road.

parking_split._note: Share of kerbside parking area occupied by cars vs two-wheelers. Assumption.

roads.name: JM Road
roads.note: Right of way 36 m (Oasis Designs). Post-redesign split assumed: wide footpaths, cycle track, organised parking. ITDP ranked it the best of 11 audited streets.

roads.name: Karve Road
roads.note: Typical arterial. Metro runs elevated overhead, so metro riders use no road surface.

roads.name: Satara Road
roads.note: BRT corridor. Space allocated to buses is not the same as space used: BRT ridership has been below capacity. ITDP ranked it 3rd of 11 on design quality, while this index finds walkers squeezed on width: the two measure different things.
